memory_candidates.content: In a Lean 4 codebase, adding @[simp] characterization lemmas does NOT improve existing proofs when those proofs use 'simp only [...]', which consults only its named lemmas. Worse, ADDING the new characterization lemma names to an existing 'simp only' list without REMOVING the syntax-unfolding lemmas (e.g. Formula.and/or/neg, which unfold a derived operator to its primitive encoding) is a verified no-op: simp rewrites subterms bottom-up, so the unfolder fires on the argument before the head-matching characterization lemma can apply, and the goal is left in the old pathological shape. The corollary for planning: a task framed as 'add an @[simp] API' is really a call-site rewrite task that the attribute merely enables, and the attribute work should be sized as a small enabling phase while the bulk of effort goes to rewriting call sites. A second, independent hazard in the same family: registering two @[simp] lemmas with identical LHS and different RHS makes the normal form an artifact of declaration order and silently strands every proof written against the loser -- pick exactly one normal form per head symbol.
